title: Remediate P2-001 schema assurance and semantic ordering
businessObjective: Close the two contract-assurance gaps identified after P2-001 completion before downstream analytics or intelligence relies on its V1 authorities.
technicalObjective: Use a bounded standards-compliant Draft 2020-12 validator to compile and exercise the committed request and result schemas, prove generated results satisfy exactly one variant, and document correlation-ID ordering as deterministic semantic validation beyond JSON Schema.
assumptions: The existing exact validator command remains admitted; this remediation does not add or alter a verifier command path.
Draft 2020-12 cannot express lexicographic array ordering, so the committed schema remains the structural authority and the pure calculator enforces the documented ordering semantic.
No production write, deployment, credential, live data, database, provider, report, recommendation, or action is authorized.
acceptanceCriteria: A bounded standards-compliant Draft 2020-12 validator dependency is declared in the root manifest and lockfile and the existing analytics validator compiles both committed schemas against the Draft 2020-12 metaschema before exercising them.

The validator accepts canonical structurally valid requests, rejects canonical structurally invalid requests, validates every calculator result it generates against the committed result schema, and rejects focused malformed result variants.

The validator proves each canonical result is accepted by exactly one of the five committed result variants and covers satisfiable `ok`, `non-comparable`, and `invalid` outcomes without broad theoretical keyword mutation.

The request schema and both analytics documents explicitly state that correlation identifiers must be unique and lexicographically ascending and that Draft 2020-12 validates their structure and uniqueness while the deterministic calculator enforces ordering semantically.

A focused regression proves the committed request schema accepts an otherwise valid request with unsorted correlation IDs while `calculateMetricComparison` deterministically returns the schema-valid `INVALID_CONTEXT` deny-style invalid result without throwing.

The calculator retains one stable public function, accepts no caller-supplied schema or dependency authority, imports no infrastructure, and all malformed inputs continue to return deterministic schema-valid invalid results without throwing.
Independent Sol QA confirms the standards-based assertions, exact-one variant behavior, semantic-ordering boundary, allowed paths, deterministic checks, evidence, and rollback before verification.
allowedCommands: npm run verify:task -- --task SUT-AIOS-P2-001-R02 --verifier-agent qa-verification --verifier-model gpt-5.6-sol --acceptance-confirmed
requiredChecks: canonical request schema acceptance and rejection
solEscalationTriggers: Any change to calculator arithmetic, reason precedence, public API, or caller authority.
Any live data, provider, report, recommendation, authorization, approval, execution, production write, payment, booking, inventory, database, RLS, migration, or workflow proposal.
Any dependency or schema behavior beyond the two identified finite remediation findings.
rollbackExpectations: Revert only the R02 dependency declaration/lock entries, focused schema descriptions, analytics validator assertions, documentation, risk entry, task state, and R02 evidence; preserve the completed P2-001 packet and historical evidence unchanged.
